Hey Voat, what was your WORST KISS EVER?

I'm 19 and she's 25.

It was one of my first jobs, I did simple office work for a sales office. They were opening up a new office and asked me to travel to it (about a 4 hour drive) to help train their office administrator - sure sounds like fun. When I arrive, there are many people training and many people getting trained for various positions. I was one of the few people that actually drove there, they basically picked the "best" person for each position they had in the country and flew them all to this new office to train the new staff.

My superior from corporate was young for her position, and probably the closest to my age. We had chatted online countless times (this is how the company communicated) and she would often give me instructions or make requests via chat. We always got along, and would always end up chatting throughout the day about random BS.

She was there that day, training. She was better looking then her little avatar picture suggested, but I didn't think anything would happen with her that day (although I would welcome it with open arms given the chance). At the end of the day we were talking about our hotel rooms, and she remarks:

"What? They didn't give you your own room, you're sharing with someone? That sucks -- here come hang out with me after work we'll get some food". I was only 19, but I knew what this meant. Green light. YES! WOW! REALLY?! Yup, I'm getting laid tonight - awesome! The first thing she hands me when I walk into her room is a screwdriver. It is very important to notice that by this point in my life, I had drank before but never more then 2 drinks and more often it was just 1. I had never been drunk before. I really like the taste of the screwdriver and she apparently really likes pouring them for me, so I have 5 more.

Keep in mind that the concept "The more alcohol I drink the more effect it will have on me" was something that I had never experienced before - so when it hit...it HIT. I stood up to go to the bed she was lying on, and I got very dizzy.

We talk for less then 10 seconds before we start kissing. This was my first time kissing a smoker, and she had just finished a cigarette. I'll never forget how that kiss felt - it was as if I was making out with a pile of ashes that had been drenched with saliva and left in a refrigerator with rotting foods around it for about a month. It was the coldest, slimiest, most disgusting tasting thing that I have had in my mouth to this day.

About as soon as my tongue touched her tongue, my 6 screwdrivers made their journey from my stomach to her mouth. She screamed, I screamed - this was disgusting. It was revolting. It was gross. There was vomit all over me. Naturally, I ran to the bathroom and closed the door and cleaned up and finished throwing up. She was knocking on the door to get in to clean up as well but I didn't let her in - In my drunk state I was upset with her for making me throw up on myself and I had to get clean, plus I didn't want a girl covered in vomit around me while I was trying to clean vomit off of myself (it seemed counterproductive).

Needless to say there was no sex that night, and gone were the days of flirting on chat all day while working.

One of the main rules of life: never have any thing to do with sex and a coworker. From flirting to everything leading up to sex.

Also: the tongue is a muscle. And my worst kiss ever was a person that used that muscle like other muscles in the body: strongly. That thing was jabbing into my mouth and going around my mouth on the outside. It wasnt too big but the force of it is very memorable.

Greene is one of the most known English authors of the twentieth century, and had an influence over an enormous range of other well-known authors. He's very far from being obscure. But you could make the case about not enough love, due to certain literary prizes passing him by.

Joe Abercrombie

If you like fantasy books like Lord of the Rings or Game of Thrones you owe it to yourself to read The First Law trilogy. There are a few seemingly cliche moments in the first book but seemingly is the key word. He also has a few books set in the same world as The First Law which are just as good. He says he's going to start writing a new trilogy soon which has me foaming at the mouth with anticipation. Seriously, check out his books.

Christopher Ruz. He has a way of setting the scene that transports you into the dark, gritty worlds he conjures up. His short stories are thought provoking and I thoroughly enjoy his fantasy novellas and novels. He has an action/mystery series published under the name D. D. Marks, but I've never read it as I prefer fantasy.

John Crowley and Gene Wolfe.

Both are incredibly literary writers, probably better prose writers than many of the more high-brow authors that get a lot of recognition, but they've been relegated to Sci-fi/Fantasy since their work contains elements of it.

Now the whole entirely-real-but-with-one-uncanny-thing is all over the place and complicated fantasy is sought out; I feel like both of these missed being literary titans outside of their respective niches and I wish more people would make noise about their (still ongoing) work.

Little, Big, by Crowley, has been one of my favorite books and has some of the most amazing writing I've encountered. The Book of the New Sun by Gene Wolfe is one of the most complicated and smartest series you'll ever go near. It's a series that rewards rereading like very few others (except the covers are some of the worst things in the history of mankind, and I like to think that these had something to do with the continued lack of mass recognition. You can't read them in public.)

I love your taste! Two of my absolute favorites as well. But Bruce Pennington's covers for the UK editions of the Book of the New Sun are, along with much of his other cover work, some of the most beautiful sci-fi/fantasy artwork that ever features on the front of books.

There's a series called "The Lost Years of Merlin" by T.A. Barron. It's young adult fantasy, and it's an excellent series. I always wondered why more people hadn't read it. It's my second-favorite fantasy series after Harry Potter.
